Repository review · 20 November 2026

Make the ASIC path reliable,
then make it easier to learn.

Four small entry scripts connect the labs to LibreLane. The first improvements should repair source preparation and define the ASIC interface; then add reproducible environments, useful run summaries and explicit viewer selection.

Reviewed basics-graphics-music main at b255c43ce4a4 · branch codex_libre_lane · LibreLane 3.0.17 at 64ef80802d3d. Official documentation and release source checked on 20 November 2026.

Start with S01–S06. A basic lab currently loses a required header during staging. Recursive flattening also makes source selection ambiguous, while the wrapper and timing settings need an explicit design contract. Fix those before tuning placement or expanding the list of supported labs.

14 suggestions shown
P0ReproducedSourcesEffort: Small

S01 Stage the complete header dependency set

The AND/OR lab reaches the LibreLane call with an incomplete source tree. The copied config.svh includes define_gowin_or_nothing.svh, but step 07 does not supply that header. Real Icarus elaboration of this staged input fails; adding only a neutral ASIC header makes the same elaboration pass.

Suggested change. Provide an ASIC-specific neutral header or remove the FPGA-specific include from the common configuration through an explicit target contract. Collect transitive headers and required shared modules; declare include directories. Do not define GOWIN for an ASIC just to silence the error.

Acceptance check. A fresh checkout stages and elaborates the basic logic lab without borrowing files from an FPGA board or an old run. A missing include is reported before the expensive physical flow starts.

Evidence: scripts/steps/07_synthesize_for_asic.source_bash:25 · labs/common/config.svh:12 · Missing-header reproduction and one-change control

P1ReproducedSourcesEffort: Medium

S02 Replace recursive flattening with an ordered source manifest

Step 07 copies every matching descendant into one src directory and ignores filelist.f and no_sources_in_this_dir. The existing unfinished UART parent lab supplies five different lab_top.sv files to the same destination. Its parent file happened to win in this run; there is no collision check or declared precedence. APS already has an ordered file list.

Suggested change. Select sources explicitly, honor exclusion markers, preserve relative paths or reject duplicate basenames, and retain package order. Use null-delimited traversal where discovery is needed. Make a lab-specific asic_top.sv an explicit override, instead of an incidental overwrite of the shared wrapper.

Acceptance check. Staging the UART parent either selects the intended top unambiguously or stops with both conflicting paths. Excluded companion files are absent; APS package order and every include path remain reproducible.

Evidence: scripts/steps/07_synthesize_for_asic.source_bash:35 · labs/5_cpu/5_5_aps/filelist.f:1 · UART collision check

P1Integration probeSourcesEffort: Medium

S03 Stage every generated ROM image and align RARS setup

The shared assembler now generates a .hex file for every selected .s, but ASIC staging copies only program.hex after assembly. In an HH CPU integration probe, riscvtest.hex was generated in run and omitted from src, although the lab configuration selects it. HH currently has ASIC templates but no step-07 launcher: this is a readiness finding, not a claimed failure of a shipped HH ASIC command.

Suggested change. Declare program inputs and generated memory outputs in the manifest. Assemble first, validate success, then stage the full declared output set with deterministic names and paths. Trigger RARS discovery for the same selected assembly set, rather than only a root program.s. Treat C/assembly toolchain preparation as a separate step from layout viewing.

Acceptance check. A fixture with two programs and one excluded companion produces exactly the two intended ROM images. Missing or stale ROM data fails before synthesis, and a lab containing only a differently named .s initializes its assembler correctly.

Evidence: scripts/steps/07_synthesize_for_asic.source_bash:50 · scripts/steps/00_setup_rars.source_bash:84 · scripts/steps/00_setup.source_bash:763 · labs/5_cpu/5_6_hh_single_cycle/prog_config.svh:4

P1Source reviewDesignEffort: Medium

S04 Define which lab interfaces the ASIC wrapper actually preserves

The shared wrapper exposes keys, switches, LEDs and seven-segment signals. It leaves audio and UART inputs/outputs disconnected, omits graphics coordinates, and passes w_gpio=0. A Verilog range such as [-1:0] is not a zero-width bus. The 109 lab/book ASIC launchers are entry points, not evidence that 109 meaningful designs have been hardened.

Suggested change. Publish a supported-lab matrix and explicit wrapper profiles: basic digital I/O first, then CPU, graphics or audio where their interfaces are deliberately exposed or tied off. Use legal widths and parameter checks. Keep lint errors enabled and review unconnected-input, width and removed-logic diagnostics; check synthesis contents, not only the exit code.

Acceptance check. For each supported profile, test interface widths and signal behavior, then verify that expected registers, memories and output logic survive synthesis. Unsupported labs explain which interface is missing.

Evidence: scripts/asic/asic_top.sv:5 · labs/2_graphics/2_1_rectangle_ellipse_parabola/lab_top.sv:40 · LibreLane lint-checker controls

P1Source reviewDesignEffort: Medium

S05 Make functional clock assumptions and timing constraints explicit

The wrapper tells labs clk_mhz=50, while the SKY130 profile constrains CLOCK_PERIOD=14 ns (about 71.43 MHz). This may be intentional timing overconstraint, but it is unexplained. There is also an external slow_clk port with no repository-specific timing contract. The clock frequency of an external chip is not generated by an SDC constraint.

Suggested change. Choose and document the operating clock; use 20 ns for a 50 MHz baseline unless a tighter target is deliberate. Propagate the matching functional parameter. Define input/output delays, reset handling and the role of slow_clk; constrain it as a clock only where it really is one. Supply reviewed PnR/signoff SDC for the supported interface.

Acceptance check. The selected operating frequency agrees with counters/UART timing. STA reports intended clocks and no unexplained unconstrained paths. Deliberate margin targets and false paths are documented individually.

Evidence: scripts/asic/sky130A_sky130_fd_sc_hd_config.tcl:5 · scripts/asic/asic_top.sv:13 · PnR and signoff SDC handling

P1ReproducedShellEffort: Small

S06 Use one quoted project path and support source archives

Synthesis recomputes the root with git rev-parse, while the viewers use the existing package_dir. A source archive fails at the Git command. A checkout path containing spaces fails in staging because paths passed to mkdir, pushd and LibreLane are unquoted; shared setup also has an unquoted cd.

Suggested change. Use the already resolved package_dir for both synthesis and viewers. Quote every path and use arrays for tool arguments. Treat Git metadata as optional provenance. Keep directory changes in subshells where possible and use a repository-relative lab identifier for future collision resistance.

Acceptance check. The same wrapper smoke checks pass in a normal checkout, a path with spaces, and an exported source tree. No unexpected directories appear beside the intended design directory.

Evidence: scripts/steps/07_synthesize_for_asic.source_bash:4 · scripts/steps/00_setup_libre_lane.source_bash:65 · scripts/steps/00_setup.source_bash:73

P2ModernizationConfigurationEffort: Medium

S07 Introduce explicit, validated PDK and per-lab configuration

The template uses Tcl and legacy variable names. It fixes a 1000 × 1000 µm die, while CPU overrides choose 500 × 500 µm. Only the SKY130 HD companion file supplies the repository clock value; another PDK/SCL can miss that file and inherit different defaults. These dimensions are policy choices, not measured area requirements.

Suggested change. Prefer a shared JSON/YAML baseline with documented per-lab overrides and explicit PDK, SCL, clock, sources and include paths. Adopt current variable names and units. Offer measured floorplan presets or utilization-driven sizing, and record the resolved configuration. Evaluate USE_SLANG for labs needing richer SystemVerilog; do not enable it globally without frontend comparisons.

Acceptance check. Configuration loading reports the chosen PDK/SCL, period, floorplan and frontend. Modernized values resolve equivalently before retuning. Existing CPU overrides continue to work or receive a documented migration.

Evidence: scripts/asic/config.tcl:3 · Configuration formats · Fanout alias · Density alias and percentage conversion · Frontend and parameter controls

P2ImprovementEnvironmentEffort: Medium

S08 Check a complete, pinned tool environment before staging

librelane_setup checks only whether a command is on PATH. LIBRELANE_PATH is prepended as a directory despite the wording “binary path.” An empty value creates an empty PATH component. The scripts do not select or record a supported LibreLane release, tool closure or PDK revision.

Suggested change. Document a pinned Nix environment as the primary route, with upstream AppImage or container alternatives. Check version and environment health before deleting/replacing staging files. Reject an empty/non-directory LIBRELANE_PATH, or introduce an explicitly named executable option. Record the LibreLane revision, Nix lock or image digest, PDK revision, SCL and source commit in a run manifest.

Acceptance check. A clean supported environment passes librelane --smoke-test. A Python-only launcher or broken tool environment receives an actionable error. Running again with the same manifest selects the same versions.

Evidence: scripts/steps/00_setup_libre_lane.source_bash:38 · Supported installation routes · PDK selection and Ciel versioning · Pinned release tool dependencies

P2ReproducedViewingEffort: Small–medium

S09 Give viewers an explicit run/state selector and clear prerequisites

Steps 08/09 open the last run and offer no wrapper-level run selection. Before synthesis, both exit with no diagnostic: their failing pushd redirects stderr to /dev/null. LibreLane’s last-run selection uses modification times; that does not establish that the run completed or represents the current RTL.

Suggested change. Check design, configuration, selected run and required ODB/DEF/GDS state before launching a viewer. Accept a run tag and optional saved state; show the selected lab/run/stage in the message. Check graphical-display availability separately from flow execution. Keep both viewer shortcuts and teach users which database they open.

Acceptance check. No-run and partial-run fixtures give useful messages. A requested older run opens exactly that run. Missing GUI/display support does not prevent a headless synthesis task.

P2ImprovementResultsEffort: Medium

S10 Summarize the exact run and its quality metrics

Step 07 prints the design directory after completion. LibreLane already produces structured results; the wrapper does not surface the exact run, timing/DRC/LVS status, area or useful viewer commands. This is an integration opportunity, not a claim that LibreLane lacks reports.

Suggested change. Capture the command and combined console log while retaining pipefail. Print the exact run directory and link a small summary to resolved settings, final views, metrics and checker results. Distinguish failed, partial and completed runs; make unavailable metrics visibly “not run” rather than zero.

Acceptance check. A successful run has traceable source/config/tool provenance and a compact result summary. A failed tool still returns its nonzero status and never prints a success banner. Do not equate a produced GDS file with independent manufacturing signoff.

P2ImprovementTeachingEffort: Medium

S11 Offer staged learning modes alongside the full Classic flow

The entry point named “synthesize” always invokes the full Classic flow. That includes substantially more than RTL synthesis. Beginners need a quick way to inspect their netlist before spending time on floorplanning, routing and verification.

Suggested change. Keep full Classic as a documented mode and add named checkpoints: lint, synthesis with structural checks, floorplan, and full layout. Use supported stop/resume controls and explicit run tags. Pair each checkpoint with the artifact and questions it teaches; do not open a layout viewer before an appropriate layout state exists.

Acceptance check. A synthesis-only exercise stops after synthesis checkers and explains which later checks have not run. Resuming a compatible run uses the recorded inputs rather than silently combining changed RTL/configuration with an old state.

S12 Add a small regression ladder tied to actual failure modes

The repository has FPGA/menu tests but no dedicated LibreLane wrapper regression. A wrapper can invoke a tool successfully while packaging the wrong files, as the stub checks in this review demonstrate. Passing Bash syntax is useful but does not validate source closure or ASIC behavior.

Suggested change. Start with cheap manifest/path/ROM/viewer/exit-status checks. Add real frontend tests for a combinational lab, a counter, and a CPU with ROM. Run a small pinned SKY130 Classic job on a suitably provisioned runner, retaining logs, resolved config and metrics. Expand coverage only after each lab has an explicit supported interface.

Acceptance check. CI detects a missing header, colliding top, excluded companion, missing ROM and swallowed tool failure. The physical test reports constrained timing and DRC/LVS outcomes; stub success is never reported as physical-flow success.

S13 Separate preparation, run retention and cleanup

Step 07 clears staged Tcl/HDL/HEX files but retains prior runs under the same design directory. The clean script still knows only the old openlane_dir/designs location. Rebuilding can therefore leave historical runs alongside different current source/config files.

Suggested change. Prepare inputs in a fresh directory, validate them, then publish the staging set. Preserve a manifest for every run. Add explicit dry-run/list and selective clean operations for LibreLane designs/runs, with a validated project-root boundary. Keep historical runs available by default and make disk usage visible.

Acceptance check. Interrupted preparation does not destroy a usable staged input set. Cleanup selects only the named lab/run and shows its target. Shared PDK caches and unrelated projects are outside its scope.

What current LibreLane changes about the recommendations

LibreLane 3.0.17 was the latest release returned during this review. Use that as a tested candidate, not a permanent “latest” dependency. The upstream documentation recommends Nix for its reproducible tool environment and also describes AppImage and Docker routes. Its smoke test is a better installation check than finding only a Python entry point on PATH. Installation options · Nix setup and smoke test.

The CLI supports named runs and stopping/resuming a sequential flow. OpenInOpenROAD opens an ODB state; OpenInKLayout uses LEF/DEF state. For reproducible viewing, select a run and, where needed, an explicit intermediate state. CLI controls · Viewer flow definitions.

# Proposed usage after source/configuration fixes; not a completed run.
librelane --flow Classic --run-tag synth-review \
  --to Checker.NetlistAssignStatements ./config.json

librelane --flow Classic --run-tag layout-review ./config.json

librelane --flow OpenInOpenROAD --run-tag layout-review ./config.json
librelane --flow OpenInKLayout --run-tag layout-review ./config.json

These are proposed CLI examples, not new wrapper options or successful commands executed during this review. A synthesis stop does not run physical signoff checks. The complete argument interface should be tested against the pinned version before exposing it to students.

Existing behavior worth preserving

  • The shared set -Eeuo pipefail propagates a failing LibreLane exit. A stub returning 23 caused the wrapper to return 23, with no success banner.
  • Lowercase openinopenroad and openinklayout are valid CLI spellings: the flow option is case-insensitive. Using canonical capitalization would improve readability, not fix a bug. CLI choice definition.
  • ASIC scripts already bypass FPGA-board selection because the common setup checks the script name. Do not add an unnecessary FPGA-board dependency. Existing board-selection guard.
  • ERROR_ON_LINTER_WARNINGS=0 matches the pinned release’s default; it does not disable fatal lint errors. Improve warning review and regression expectations rather than claim all lint is switched off. Separate warning/error controls.

An implementation order with reviewable stopping points

Phase 1 · Reliable inputs

S01, S02, S03, S06

Fix header closure and path quoting, then introduce an explicit source/program manifest. Start with basic logic and a counter; use the CPU probe to validate program staging before declaring CPU support.

Gate: deterministic source inventory, legal paths, no collisions and correct ROM contents. Fast wrapper/frontend checks pass.

Phase 2 · Explicit design

S04, S05, S07, S08

Define supported wrapper profiles, clocks, constraints, PDK/SCL and environment pins. Modernize configuration without changing its meaning before tuning area or timing.

Gate: a real pinned basic-lab flow succeeds and its netlist, clocks and resolved configuration match the intended design.

Phase 3 · Useful results

S09, S10, S11

Add explicit run/state selection, visible failure reasons, a result summary and optional teaching checkpoints. Keep the existing full-flow shortcut.

Gate: partial, failed, old and complete runs are distinguishable; the selected viewer opens the intended state.

Phase 4 · Maintain coverage

S12, S13, S14

Make the regression ladder repeatable, add deliberate retention/cleanup, and document the tested student workflow. Include the cheap checks from phase 1 from the beginning.

Gate: a fresh supported environment follows the guide; CI catches the regressions without treating unrun physical checks as passed.

Evidence and limits

The reproduction script copies the repository’s scripts and representative labs into disposable fixtures. It leaves the reviewed worktree unchanged. Stub commands record arguments and create synthetic ROM outputs; they do not emulate Yosys, OpenROAD, RARS instruction semantics or a PDK.

error: Unable to find the root module "asic_top" in the Verilog source.

Adding only a neutral define_gowin_or_nothing.svh to that disposable source directory changed Icarus’s result from failure to success. This establishes the packaging problem; it does not establish downstream physical-flow correctness.

Scope qualifications

  • The HH CPU integration probe supplies the unchanged common step-07 launcher because that lab does not yet ship one. It confirms a missing generated image when that path is enabled.
  • The UART collision probe uses its existing launcher. Multiple different sources target one output filename; the parent lab_top.sv won on this filesystem. No particular losing top is asserted as the universal result.
  • The no-run viewer failures are silent because pushd redirects both output streams. The recommended preflight should report the missing design/run explicitly.
  • There are no duplicate lab basenames among the 109 scanned lab/book launchers today. A path-derived design ID is future-proofing, not a claimed current design-directory collision.
  • Clock, wrapper, PDK and frontend proposals still require a real pinned LibreLane run and appropriate design tests.
